sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《20多岁的心理学》，在这个播客中，我们探讨20多岁时经历的一些重大人生变化

sentences.en: and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 和过渡期，以及它们对我们心理的影响。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, dive into the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何地，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们要深入探讨20多岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Today, let's cut to the chase.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们开门见山。

sentences.en: We're going to be talking about crying.
sentences.zh: 我们要谈谈哭泣。

sentences.en: It might seem a little bit insignificant to be devoting a whole episode to this.
sentences.zh: 专门用一整期节目来讨论这个话题，似乎有点微不足道。

sentences.en: It might seem a bit strange when it comes to our 20s.
sentences.zh: 当谈到20多岁时，这似乎有点奇怪。

sentences.en: I think that a lot of us try to avoid crying.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们很多人都在试图避免哭泣。

sentences.en: But sometimes there is no better feeling than just having a solid moment to let yourself be in pain, to experience a little bit of self-pity, and to let it all out through tears.
sentences.zh: 但有时，没有什么比给自己留出一个踏实的时刻，让自己沉浸在痛苦中，体验一点点自怜，并通过泪水将一切宣泄出来更好的感觉了。

sentences.en: And sometimes nothing feels more frustrating than wanting so badly to cry and have that physical outlet for your emotions and being unable to.
sentences.zh: 有时，没有什么比极度想哭却无法获得这种情感的生理宣泄更让人沮丧的了。

sentences.en: It can feel like something within us is blocked, something about us is defective or faulty because we're not feeling things deeply enough
sentences.zh: 这会让人觉得我们内心深处有什么东西被堵住了，或者我们自身有什么缺陷或故障，因为我们没有足够深刻地感受事物，

sentences.en: or to the point where we can let it all out and have this like physical expression of what is occurring internally.
sentences.zh: 或者没有达到那种可以释放一切，并对内在发生的事情进行生理表达的程度。

sentences.en: And I really get that.
sentences.zh: 我真的很理解这一点。

sentences.en: It can leave us with a lot of, I think, frustration and almost like anger at ourselves and just this like longing for a good old-fashioned sob.
sentences.zh: 我想，这会给我们留下很多挫败感，甚至是对自己的愤怒，以及对一场痛痛快快大哭的渴望。

sentences.en: The truth of the matter is our 20s are really freaking hard.
sentences.zh: 事实是，我们的20多岁真的非常艰难。

sentences.en: Being human is hard.
sentences.zh: 做人很难。

sentences.en: Life is hard.
sentences.zh: 生活很难。

sentences.en: We are all going to go through difficult moments and times in our lives where we lose people.
sentences.zh: 我们都会经历人生中艰难的时刻，经历失去亲人的时候。

sentences.en: We are frustrated by life.
sentences.zh: 我们会被生活挫败。

sentences.en: We're having a really rough time at work.
sentences.zh: 我们在工作中过得很艰难。

sentences.en: Like our boss is an asshole.
sentences.zh: 比如我们的老板是个混蛋。

sentences.en: And being able to release all that stress, that grief, that anger, that sadness is one of the good parts about being human and having that huge catalogue of emotional expressions
sentences.zh: 能够释放所有的压力、悲伤、愤怒和痛苦，是作为人类并拥有庞大情感表达库的好处之一，

sentences.en: and ability to feel emotions.
sentences.zh: 也是感受情绪的能力。

sentences.en: When we feel detached from that ability, and it happens every now and again, we, I think, feel almost under control, under the control of our emotions.
sentences.zh: 当我们感到与这种能力脱节时——这种情况偶尔会发生——我认为我们几乎会感到自己被情绪所控制。

sentences.en: And we feel like there is this pent-up energy inside of us that has nowhere to go but up and into our brain and cause us more stress and more fear and more anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得内心有一种压抑的能量，无处可去，只能向上涌入大脑，导致我们产生更多的压力、恐惧和焦虑。

sentences.en: And tears serve a purpose.
sentences.zh: 眼泪是有目的的。

sentences.en: Sometimes they serve as an outlet.
sentences.zh: 有时它们是一种宣泄渠道。

sentences.en: There is nothing better.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比这更好的了。

sentences.en: So for anyone who is feeling a little bit emotionally repressed at the moment, who is finding that they can't even cry in the moments they want nothing more than,
sentences.zh: 所以，对于任何此刻感到情绪有些压抑，发现自己在最想哭的时候却哭不出来的人，

sentences.en: that's what we're going to discuss today.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: We're going to examine some of the reasons psychology and science tells us we need to cry, why we can't cry from emotional suppression to medications or shock,
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨心理学和科学告诉我们为什么需要哭泣，为什么我们哭不出来——从情绪压抑到药物或休克，

sentences.en: and how we can get back in touch with our big emotions rather than being scared of them.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何重新与我们的强烈情绪建立联系，而不是害怕它们。

sentences.en: So let us get into it.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们开始吧。

sentences.en: To start off with, why do we actually need to cry?
sentences.zh: 首先，我们为什么真的需要哭泣？

sentences.en: Obviously, if we can do it, evolution tells us that it must have served a purpose.
sentences.zh: 显然，如果我们能做到这一点，进化论告诉我们它一定是有目的的。

sentences.en: Before we talk about that, let's just briefly mention some of the anatomy for a second.
sentences.zh: 在讨论这个问题之前，让我们先简要提一下解剖学知识。

sentences.en: Each of us is born with two tear ducts in each of our eyes, and they have two openings, one on the upper eyelid, one on the, like, in the inner eyelid.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人出生时，每只眼睛都有两个泪管，它们有两个开口，一个在上眼睑，一个在内眼睑。

sentences.en: We all, you know what I'm talking about, close to the bridge of the nose.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道，就是靠近鼻梁的地方。

sentences.en: Now, crying doesn't just occur for emotional reasons.
sentences.zh: 哭泣不仅仅是因为情绪原因。

sentences.en: There are actually three different types of tears.
sentences.zh: 实际上有三种不同类型的眼泪。

sentences.en: We have basal tears, reflex tears, and emotional tears.
sentences.zh: 我们有基础泪、反射泪和情绪泪。

sentences.en: Basal tears, they wash away dirt and germs and yucky things, keeping us from getting an infection, going blind, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 基础泪可以冲走灰尘、细菌和脏东西，防止我们感染、失明等等。

sentences.en: Reflex tears are what occur when something harmful gets in our eye like a bug, or when we're cutting onion.
sentences.zh: 反射泪是当有害物质进入眼睛时产生的，比如虫子，或者切洋葱时。

sentences.en: It's responsive to something coming from the environment.
sentences.zh: 它是对来自环境的刺激的反应。

sentences.en: And then finally, we have emotional tears.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们有情绪泪。

sentences.en: Emotional tears are a lot more complicated than basal and reflex tears, which I'm sure we kind of all assumed at this point.
sentences.zh: 情绪泪比基础泪和反射泪复杂得多，我相信大家对此都已经有所了解。

sentences.en: But the thing about emotional tears is that they are not automatic.
sentences.zh: 但情绪泪的关键在于它们不是自动产生的。

sentences.en: In order to cry, our limbic system, the part of our brain that regulates our emotions, that part of our brain has to be activated and send signals to our glands to produce tears.
sentences.zh: 为了哭泣，我们的边缘系统——大脑中调节情绪的部分——必须被激活，并向腺体发送信号以产生眼泪。

sentences.en: And in those tears contains a bunch of other proteins and hormones that we don't find in our everyday basal or reflex tears.
sentences.zh: 这些眼泪中含有许多我们在日常基础泪或反射泪中找不到的其他蛋白质和激素。

sentences.en: Things like potassium, prolactin, which also helps us produce milk.
sentences.zh: 比如钾、催乳素（也有助于我们分泌乳汁）。

sentences.en: And finally, the big one, stress hormones like cortisol.
sentences.zh: 最后，最重要的一种，压力荷尔蒙，比如皮质醇。

sentences.en: This is probably our first clue that we're dealing with something a little bit bigger when we need to cry.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我们的第一个线索，即当我们想哭时，我们处理的事情要大得多。

sentences.en: It's a lot more psychological than just physical.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是生理上的，更多是心理上的。

sentences.en: That's because most evolutionary researchers will tell you that crying serves a purpose.
sentences.zh: 这是因为大多数进化研究人员会告诉你，哭泣是有目的的。

sentences.en: Actually, it serves a number of important functions that all have something to do with how we feel emotion and how we connect to others through mental,
sentences.zh: 实际上，它具有许多重要的功能，都与我们如何感受情绪以及如何通过心理、

sentences.en: physical and emotional expressions of pain.
sentences.zh: 生理和情感上的痛苦表达与他人建立联系有关。

sentences.en: So, firstly, when you are in emotional or physical pain, crying can actually make you feel really good.
sentences.zh: 首先，当你处于情感或身体痛苦中时，哭泣实际上能让你感觉非常好。

sentences.en: It can actually provide real physical relief from that pain.
sentences.zh: 它实际上可以提供真正的生理缓解，减轻那种痛苦。

sentences.en: When you cry, your body releases hormones such as endorphins and oxytocin, the same chemical structures that we see in pain relievers and opioids.
sentences.zh: 当你哭泣时，你的身体会释放内啡肽和催产素等激素，这些化学结构与止痛药和阿片类药物中的相同。

sentences.en: That is why a big sob feels just so good.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么大哭一场感觉如此之好。

sentences.en: Even though that might seem counterintuitive because we often associate it with sadness and pain, really this act is telling your body that something is wrong,
sentences.zh: 尽管这看起来可能有些反直觉，因为我们经常把它与悲伤和痛苦联系在一起，但实际上这种行为是在告诉你的身体，有什么地方不对劲，

sentences.en: something has triggered this reaction and it needs to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 有什么东西触发了这种反应，它需要对此采取行动。

sentences.en: So it fires up all these pleasurable neurotransmitters and hormones to counteract whatever painful thing is bothering us.
sentences.zh: 所以它会激发所有这些令人愉悦的神经递质和激素，来抵消困扰我们的任何痛苦事物。

sentences.en: There is a really interesting article by Harvard Health that talks about this and it also speaks on how crying provides an emotional catharsis.
sentences.zh: 哈佛健康（Harvard Health）有一篇非常有趣的文章讨论了这一点，它还谈到了哭泣如何提供情感宣泄。

sentences.en: It gives big emotions somewhere to go that isn't just running around in our brain in an endless ruminating loop.
sentences.zh: 它为强烈的情绪提供了一个去处，而不是让它们在大脑中无休止地循环反刍。

sentences.en: So it's really interesting because that is not a new idea, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这非常有趣，因为这不是一个新想法，对吧？

sentences.en: Even back in a lot of the ancient civilizations, the Greeks, the Romans, they almost saw our tears as having a healing capacity.
sentences.zh: 甚至在许多古代文明中，希腊人、罗马人，他们几乎认为我们的眼泪具有治愈能力。

sentences.en: They would drain us of something negative.
sentences.zh: 它们会排走我们体内负面的东西。

sentences.en: They would purify us and not only has that really like continued to stand but now there have been a lot more papers and a lot more research into this that is proving
sentences.zh: 它们会净化我们，不仅这种观点一直流传下来，而且现在有了更多的论文和研究证明，

sentences.en: that those initial conceptions and ideas were actually pretty close to the scientific truth.
sentences.zh: 那些最初的构想和想法实际上非常接近科学事实。

sentences.en: Now, crying isn't the only way to do this.
sentences.zh: 当然，哭泣并不是做到这一点的唯一方式。

sentences.en: You know, exercise is another way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，运动是另一种方式。

sentences.en: Displacement, as Freud would call it, is also another way taking your pain out on others but it is the one that seems most accepted and socialized.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德所说的“置换”也是另一种方式，即把痛苦发泄在别人身上，但哭泣似乎是最被接受和社交化的方式。

sentences.en: Of course, if your pet died, you know, you're going to cry.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你的宠物死了，你知道，你会哭。

sentences.en: People accept that as part of the sadness.
sentences.zh: 人们接受这是悲伤的一部分。

sentences.en: If someone yells at you or you have this really big emotional blow-up or a conflict, again, it seems like the most natural reaction to a painful or uncomfortable situation,
sentences.zh: 如果有人对你大喊大叫，或者你发生了非常大的情绪爆发或冲突，同样，这似乎是对痛苦或不舒服情况最自然的反应，

sentences.en: crying in this way can also have a self-soothing effect.
sentences.zh: 以这种方式哭泣也可以起到自我安抚的作用。

sentences.en: So, this was a finding published by a 2014 study that noticed when people cry, this very act also activated their parasympathetic nervous system which helps us relax and once again
sentences.zh: 这是一项2014年的研究发现，该研究注意到当人们哭泣时，这种行为本身也激活了副交感神经系统，这有助于我们放松，再一次，

sentences.en: we get that intense distress kind of out of the way through the act of crying.
sentences.zh: 我们通过哭泣的行为把那种强烈的痛苦排解掉了。

sentences.en: when we activate our parasympathetic nervous system a whole bunch of other things occur in our body.
sentences.zh: 当我们激活副交感神经系统时，我们的身体会发生很多其他变化。

sentences.en: Our heart rate begins to slow down, we begin to feel quite tired and also all that emotion seems and that fear really seems to clear.
sentences.zh: 我们的心率开始减慢，我们开始感到相当疲倦，而且所有的情绪和恐惧似乎真的消散了。

sentences.en: So, we're able to think more rationally and from a place of I don't want to say peace but from a place of calm.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们能够更理性地思考，从一个——我不想说是和平，但从一个冷静的地方出发。

sentences.en: It's also why after crying you might feel really exhausted or drowsy maybe even peaceful you have involuntarily activated this very important part of your nervous system
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么哭泣后你可能会感到非常疲惫或昏昏欲睡，甚至感到平静，因为你无意中激活了神经系统中这个非常重要的部分，

sentences.en: but also you've drained a lot of that energy that was keeping you tense and sad and stressed.
sentences.zh: 而且你也排出了很多让你紧张、悲伤和压力的能量。

sentences.en: Now there's been a bit of preliminary research that has suggested that crying the reason why it makes us feel this way is because the very act of crying releases stress hormones
sentences.zh: 现在有一些初步研究表明，哭泣之所以让我们有这种感觉，是因为哭泣的行为本身通过产生眼泪释放了压力荷尔蒙，

sentences.en: through the production of tears meaning that there is less of that stress hormone particularly cortisol to go around in the body.
sentences.zh: 这意味着体内循环的压力荷尔蒙（特别是皮质醇）减少了。

sentences.en: I'm going to like just you know I wanted to mention that but I would also say there probably needs to be a bit more research.
sentences.zh: 我只是想提一下这一点，但我也会说可能还需要更多的研究。

sentences.en: I don't really see how a few millimeters of tears can have that much impact on the stress response of a 60 kilo
sentences.zh: 我真的看不出几毫米的眼泪怎么能对一个60公斤的人的压力反应产生那么大的影响，

sentences.en: 100 kilo
150 kilo human like it seems quite negligible but that is another explanation and the final one as to why we cry has a lot to do with
sentences.zh: 150公斤的人，这看起来相当微不足道，但这是另一种解释，而我们哭泣的最后一个原因与我们的社会进化有很大关系。

sentences.en: our social evolution so one of the first things that babies do when they are born is cry obviously that's to get a lot of the fluid out of their lungs but it's also
sentences.zh: 所以婴儿出生时做的第一件事就是哭，显然这是为了排出肺部的液体，但这也是为了引起注意，

sentences.en: to get attention and then they pretty much don't stop crying
sentences.zh: 然后他们几乎就不会停止哭泣，

sentences.en: ever like even as humans we don't stop crying but especially when we're babies like babies cry a whole lot and the reason why is because crying is what we would call
sentences.zh: 永远不会，即使作为人类我们也不会停止哭泣，但特别是当我们是婴儿时，婴儿哭得非常多，原因就是哭泣是我们所说的

sentences.en: an attachment behavior it serves as a signal to those around us to comfort us it draws people's attention to us because when they hear those cries that automatically
sentences.zh: 依恋行为，它作为一种信号向周围的人寻求安慰，它吸引人们的注意力，因为当他们听到这些哭声时，会自动

sentences.en: causes this association with distress and that acknowledgement of distress activates the part of our brain that deals with empathy and that is what motivates us to help someone
